subject: Arabic
specVersion: Issue 1, April 2017 (as stated in the specification PDF text read); first teaching September 2017, first assessment June 2019
statusNote: Replaces the earlier UK GCSE 1AA0 (foreign-language) file. The correct qualification is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Arabic 4AA1, which is a FIRST LANGUAGE qualification: all work is in Arabic and candidates must already read and write Arabic at first-language level. It is not a foreign-language course, so the KS3 Arabic programme (beginner level) does not prepare pupils directly for it. Opened: the 4AA1 specification PDF only, read through a page-summarising fetch tool, not page by page. The Pearson qualification page, sample assessment materials, mark schemes and the current exam-materials listing were not opened. Search results showed 4AA1 exam papers dated up to August 2025, which suggests the qualification is current, but this was not confirmed. Year and term allocation is a recommended sequence.

sources.title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Arabic (First Language) 4AA1 specification (PDF)

years: Years 10 to 11 (linear two-year course, all papers at the end)

assessment.title: Reading, Summary and Grammar
assessment.content: All ten topics; Part One Reading 49 marks, Part Two Summary 6 marks, Part Three Grammar 20 marks
assessment.format: Part One: two text extracts with four questions each, then a comparison of the texts (Q4 and Q8 worth 10, Q9 worth 15). Part Two: summarise a third text (6 marks). Part Three: grammar questions (20 marks).

assessment.title: Writing
assessment.format: Choose two of three titles, 25 marks each (15 for communication and content, 10 for application and accuracy of language); about 300 words each is advised, not enforced

nonExam: None: 100% external assessment. There is no speaking or listening component. Papers are in Arabic only, with January and June series.

aos.desc: Read and understand texts; interpret ideas; explain writers' techniques; compare texts; summarise
Write effectively and imaginatively for purpose and audience; organise text; spell accurately
Show understanding of grammatical terms and structures; manipulate and analyse language

units.title: Grammar: nouns, case and the noun phrase
points: Nominative, accusative and genitive case
Noun declension, definiteness, gender and number including dual and broken or weak plurals
Diptotes, Idafa, apposition, la of absolute negation, the five nouns
Adjective agreement and position; comparative and superlative

units.title: Grammar: sentences, pronouns and particles
points: Equational sentences; kana and its sisters; inna and its sisters
Demonstratives, relative and emphatic pronouns, place and time adverbs
Prepositions, coordinating and subordinating conjunctions, interrogatives
Vocative, kam, exception particle, hamza of inna and anna

units.title: Grammar: verbs and numbers
points: Verb conjugation across strong, doubled, weak, hamzated and impersonal verbs
Perfect and imperfect moods; active and passive voice; imperative; conditional
Participles, verbal nouns, verbs of praise and criticism, emotion and beginning
Cardinal and ordinal numbers, agreement with nouns, months and calendars

commandWords.meaning: The specification read does not give a command-word table; questions use Arabic task wording

skills: Reading: scan, interpret and infer explicit and implicit meaning, select textual evidence
Analyse how writers use linguistic and structural techniques for effect (Q4 and Q8, 10 marks each)
Compare two texts on ideas and techniques (Q9, 15 marks)
Summarise the main points of a short text clearly
Grammar: decline nouns and adjectives, conjugate verbs, parse, rewrite keeping meaning
Writing for purpose and audience: argue, narrate, describe, persuade, inform, explain
Writing forms: discursive essay, narrative, description, letter, article, email, speech, leaflet
Accurate spelling, wide vocabulary and varied basic and complex structures (for example cognate accusative, tamyiz, hal)

prerequisites.from: First-language Arabic reading and writing fluency (no beginner pathway)
G1 Nouns, case and the noun phrase
Reading practice across T1 to T5

contextNote: 4AA1 is a first-language qualification taken in Arabic only, so pupils need first-language reading and writing fluency before starting. If the school's pupils are learners of Arabic as a foreign language, the board's International GCSE does not offer a matching foreign-language Arabic route in the pages opened; confirm entry options with Pearson.
